newsitem.headline: NOTICE OF SALE - Bronson, Mich.

text.p: OFFICIAL NOTICE OF SALE
City of Bronson
County of Branch, State of Michigan
Water Supply and Sewage Disposal System
Revenue Bonds, Series 1997
SEALED BIDS for the purchase of the above bonds will be received by the undersigned at the office of the City Clerk located at 141 S. Matteson St., Bronson, Michigan 49028-1396 Thursday, the
8th day of May, 1997,
until 4:00 o'clock p.m., Eastern Daylight Time, at which tim place said bids will be publicly opened and read. In the

alternative, sealed bids for the purchase of the above bonds also be received until the same time on the same date at the offices of the Municipal Advisory Council of Michigan, 1445 National Building, Detroit, Michigan 48226, at which time an place said bids will be simultaneously opened and read. The Council will meet on that date, to consider the award or rejection of bids.

BOND DETAILS: The bonds will be issued in fully-registered of the denomination of $5,000 or multiples thereof not excee for each maturity the aggregate principal amount of maturity, dated as of May 1, 1997, numbered in order of registration, and will bear interest from their date payable October 1, 1997, and semiannually thereafter.
The bonds will mature on the 1st day of April of the years follows:
25,000 1999 to 2002, inclusive;

PRIOR OPTIONAL REDEMPTION: Bonds of this issue maturing in years 1998 to 2007, inclusive, are not subject to optional redemption prior to maturity. Bonds or portions of bonds in multiples of $5,000, maturing in the years 2008 through 2012 inclusive, shall be subject to redemption, at the option of City, in such order as the City shall determine and within a maturity by lot, on any interest payment date on or after Ap 1, 2007, at par and accrued interest to the date fixed for redemption.

Notice of redemption of any bond or portion thereof shall b given by the transfer agent at least thirty (30) days prior the date fixed for redemption by mail to the registered owne the registered address shown on the registration books kept the transfer agent. Bonds shall be called for redemption in multiples of $5,000 and any bond of a denomination of more t $5,000 shall be treated as representing the number of bonds obtained by dividing the denomination of the bond by $5,000 such bond may be redeemed in part. Notice of redemption for

bond redeemed in part shall state that upon surrender o to be redeemed a new bond or bonds in aggregate principal am equal to the unredeemed portion of the bonds surrendered sha issued to the registered owner thereof. No further interest bond or portion thereof called for redemption shall accrue a the date fixed for redemption, whether presented for redempt or not, provided funds are on hand with the transfer agent t redeem the bond or portion thereof.

INTEREST RATE AND BIDDING DETAILS: The bonds shall bear int at a rate or rates not exceeding 8% per annum, to be fixed b bids therefor, expressed in multiples of 1/8 or 1/20 of 1%, both. The interest on any one bond shall be at one rate onl all bonds maturing in any one year must carry the same inter rate. THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE HIGHEST AND LOWEST RATES B THE BONDS SHALL NOT EXCEED 3%. No proposal for the purchase less than all of the bonds or at a price less than 98/% of t par value will be considered.

TRANSFER AGENT AND REGISTRATION: Principal and interest sha payable at the corporate trust office of First of America Ba Michigan, N.A., Birmingham, Michigan, or such other transfer agent as the City may thereafter designate by notice mailed the registered owners of the bonds not less than 60 days pri any interest payment date. Interest shall be paid by check draft mailed to the registered owners of the bonds as shown the registration books of the City on the 15th day of the mo preceding the interest payment date. The bonds will
transferable only upon the registration books of the City ke the transfer agent.

PURPOSE AND SECURITY: The bonds are issued under the provis of Act 94, Public Acts of Michigan, 1933, as amended, and ce Ordinances of the City, for the purpose of defraying the cos acquiring and constructing additions, extensions and improve to the City's Water Supply and Sewage Disposal System (the "System"). The bonds are payable solely and only from the n revenues of the System and any additions thereto, and a stat first lien on said revenues has been established by said Ordinances. The bonds and said lien are of equal standing w the City's Water Supply and Sewage Disposal System Revenue B in the outstanding principal amount of $791,000 (the "Outsta Bonds"). The City has covenanted and agreed to fix and main at all times while any of such bonds shall be outstanding su rates for service furnished by the System as shall be suffic to provide for payment of the necessary expenses of operatio maintenance and administration of the System, of the princip and interest on all of said bonds when due, to maintain and increase a bond reserve account therefor, and to provide for other expenditures and funds for the System as are required said Ordinances. The City has covenanted to charge and coll sufficient rates and charges each year so as to produce net revenues equal to at least 110% of annual debt service on th Bonds and the Outstanding Bonds.
The rights or remedies of bondholders may be affected by bankruptcy, insolvency, fraudulent conveyance or other laws affecting creditors' rights generally now existing or hereaf
enacted and by the application of general principles of including those relating to equitable subordination.

ADDITIONAL BONDS: For the terms upon which additional bonds equal standing with the bonds of this issue and the Outstand Bonds as to the net revenues of the System may be issued, reference is made to the above described Ordinances.

GOOD FAITH: A certified or cashier's check drawn upon an incorporated bank or trust company or a Financial Surety Bon the amount of $10,000, and payable to the order of the Treas of the City, is required for each bid as a guarantee of good faith on the part of the bidder, to be forfeited as a portio the City's damages if such bid be accepted and the bidder fa to take up and pay for the bonds. If a check is used, it mu accompany each bid. If a Financial Surety Bond is used, it be from an insurance company licenses to issue such a bond i State of Michigan and such Bond must be submitted to the Cit the Municipal Advisory Council of Michigan at least one hour prior to the opening of the bids. The Financial Surety Bond identify each bidder whose good faith deposit is guaranteed such Financial Surety Bond. If the bonds are awarded to a b utilizing a Financial Surety Bond, then that purchaser (the "Purchaser") is required to submit its good faith deposit to City or its financial advisor in the form of a cashier's che (or wire transfer such amount as instructed by the City or i financial advisor in the form of a cashier's check not later Noon, prevailing Eastern Time, on the next business day foll the award. If such good faith deposit is not received by th time, the Financial Surety Bond may be drawn by the City to satisfy the good faith deposit requirement. The good faith deposit will be applied to the purchase price of the bonds. the event the Purchaser fails to honor its accepted bid, the faith deposit will be retained by the City. No interest sha allowed on the good faith check and checks of the unsuccessf bidders will be returned to each bidder's representative or UPS - Next Day Air Service. The good faith check of the
successful bidder will be cashed and payment for the balance the purchase price of the bonds shall be made at the closing

AWARD OF BONDS: The bonds will be awarded to the bidder wh bid produces the lowest interest cost computed by determinin the rate or rates specified in the bid, the total dollar val all interest on the bonds from June 1, 1997, to their maturi and deducting therefrom any premium or adding thereto any discount.

LEGAL OPINION: Bids shall be conditioned upon the approvin opinion of Miller, Canfield, Paddock and Stone, P.L.C., atto of Detroit, Michigan, a copy of which opinion will be printe the reverse side of each bond, and the original of which wil furnished without expense to the purchaser of the bonds at t delivery thereof. The fees of Miller, Canfield, Paddock and Stone, P.L.C. for services rendered in connection with such approving opinion are expected to be paid from bond proceeds Except to the extent necessary to issue their approving opin as to validity of the above bonds, Miller, Canfield, Paddock Stone, P.L.C. has not been requested to examine or review an

not examined or reviewed any financial documents, state materials that have been or may be furnished in connection w the authorization, issuance or marketing of the bonds, and accordingly will not express any opinion with respect to the accuracy or completeness of any such financial docume statements or materials.
DELIVERY OF BONDS: The City will furnish bonds ready for execution at its expense. Bonds will be delivered without

expense to the purchaser at such place as may agreed upon. usual closing documents, including a certificate that litigation is pending affecting the issuance of the bonds, w be delivered at the time of the delivery of the bonds. If t bonds are not tendered for delivery by twelve o'clock noon, prevailing Eastern Time, on the 45th day following the date sale, or the first business day thereafter if said 45th day not a business day, the successful bidder may on that day, o time thereafter until delivery of the bonds, withdraw his proposal by serving notice of cancellation, in writing, on t undersigned in which event the City shall promptly return th good faith deposit. Payment for the bonds shall be made in immediately available funds. Accrued interest to the date o delivery of the bonds shall be paid by the purchaser at the of delivery. Unless the purchaser furnishes the transfer ag with a list giving the denominations and names in which it w to have the certificates issued at least 5 business days aft the sale of the bonds, the bonds will be delivered in the fo a single certificate for each maturity registered in the nam the purchaser.

TAX EXEMPTION: In the opinion of bond counsel, assumi compliance with certain covenants by the City, the bonds wil exempt from taxation in the State of Michigan and from feder income tax subject, in both cases, to certain except described in bond counsel's opinion.

CUSIP NUMBERS: CUSIP identification numbers will be printed the bonds, but neither the failure to print the numbers nor error with respect thereto shall constitute cause for refusa the purchaser to accept delivery of the bonds. All expenses relation to the printing of CUSIP numbers shall be paid for the City except that the CUSIP Service Bureau charge for the assignment of numbers shall be the responsibility of and pai by the purchaser.
QUALIFIED TAX EXEMPT OBLIGATIONS: The City HAS designated t bonds as "QUALIFIED TAX EXEMPT OBLIGATIONS" for purposes of deduction of interest expense by financial institutions.

CERTIFICATION: The successful bidder will be required furnish, prior to the delivery of the bonds, a certificate i form acceptable to bond counsel as to the "issue price" of t bonds within the meaning of Section 1273 of the Internal Rev Code of 1986, as amended.
OFFICIAL STATEMENT: Because of the size of the bond issue, City will not be preparing either a preliminary or final off statement for the Bonds.
THE RIGHT IS RESERVED TO REJECT ANY OR ALL BIDS.
ENVELOPES containing the bids should be plainly
"Proposal for Revenue Bonds".
Karen Smith
City Clerk, City of Bronson
(From The Bond Buyer)
